findings: Official DuckDB 1.5 evidence directly requires parentheses around a literal dot-call receiver and documents the parser failure. The current case, replay, oracle, and promotion share execution-input hash 6766d144fceadebf73990d7f95c7dfdda9717ab599898338d7913cf5ee5b9dd0; DuckDB 1.5.5 reproduced the error and returned exactly DB ERROR after the fix.

Official compatibility evidence says DuckDB identifiers are fully case-insensitive while their case is preserved. The current replay and promotion match case input hash 59b76bd3eed839378c25e3ed6866d5b247aeb1c7e17362fb51f4383f5b65223d; 1.5.5 rejected duplicate Key/key and the repaired schema-state oracle proves exactly two unambiguous INTEGER columns.

DuckDB 1.1.0 official release evidence directly documents the new multirow scalar-subquery error, its prior arbitrary-row behavior, and array as the all-results repair. ORDER BY makes [10, 11] deterministic; this exact-version case has no 1.5.5 oracle or promotion and truthfully records both forms as unexecuted documentation-only verification.

DuckDB 1.3.0 official release evidence contains the same *COLUMNS() cast binder failure, introduces UNPACK, and shows the repaired VARCHAR list [21, 1.234]. This exact-version case has no 1.5.5 oracle or promotion and its documentation-only verification makes no execution claim.

Official PostgreSQL-compatibility evidence documents DuckDB's lack of primary-key functional-dependency inference for GROUP BY and the matching binder error. The case, replay, and promotion share input hash 4bf39587abe73d320f294885e3731afe7a9e2f39418be803f7411943e42890b8; the explicit grouping repair returned the exact two ordered id-label-count rows in the structured oracle.

Official NULL evidence states that every equality comparison with NULL yields NULL and prescribes IS NULL for the missing-value test. Input hash 91785697b1c9efee7491d246dc29b7faa11ffb5cb330c996ecc4707c90c395bd is identical across case, replay, and promotion; the original returned no rows and the repair selected exactly order_id 1, matching the scalar oracle.

Official ENUM evidence documents the out-of-domain explicit-cast conversion failure. Input hash 569acc7d7a5d6da71724b12708ff13f778fed47b8ad901d3ab6be49df09803ba matches the case, replay, and promotion; DuckDB 1.5.5 reproduced the error and TRY_CAST returned exactly NULL, as required by the scalar oracle.

DuckDB 0.10.0 official release evidence documents the DATE-versus-VARCHAR binder failure, explains the changed literal binding rules, and requires an explicit cast. Casting the text to DATE makes the comparison false as intended; this exact-version case has no 1.5.5 oracle or promotion and truthfully remains documentation-only.

Official date-format evidence shows the same invalid-month strptime error and directs callers to try_strptime for NULL-on-failure behavior. Input hash 86f62defb87028c26c9874ed2752f284f537eff766ab5f4d7a4574fe6fb3ed2e matches case, replay, and promotion; 1.5.5 reproduced the error and the fixed scalar-null oracle passed exactly.

Official DROP documentation shows that view dependencies are not tracked, DROP TABLE ... RESTRICT leaves the view invalid, and the next read raises the stated missing-table error; dropping the view first directly prevents that state. A current replay with matching input hash 7c1205e28a6cd9b61987da68edeb694b25bf12c7db9813fed140e63bd31b6d7b reproduced the behavior, but DEV0246 is explicitly excluded from the structured-oracle promotion ledger, so the case truthfully retains its narrower documentation-only claim.
